papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are fundamental techniques for enabling the deployment of large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, addressing the critical challenge of reducing model size while maintaining predictive performance. This review synthesizes recent advances in distillation techniques, compression methodologies, and their applications across various deep learning domains.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have become central tools for shrinking large neural networks while retaining much of their predictive performance. Researchers have adapted KD beyond classification to tasks such as object detection, generative modeling, machine translation, and sequence-to-sequence systems, and have explored many variants including feature imitation, teacher ensembles, sample selection, communication-efficient distributed protocols, and robustness-aware distillation. Empirical work shows KD can yield substantial savings in parameter count, memory, and runtime while often preserving accuracy; however, task-specific challenges, teacher-student mismatches, and distributional or adversarial vulnerabilities require modified objectives, architectures, or training curricula to transfer the right form of “dark” knowledge. The field is moving toward methods that (a) shape teacher outputs or training so distilled information is student-friendly, (b) target intermediate features and decision boundaries rather than only logits, and (c) adapt to resource- and privacy-constrained settings such as federated or few-shot compression.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: TRILLsson: Distilled Universal Paralinguistic Speech Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervision have dramatically improved the quality of speech representations. However, deployment of state-of-the-art embedding models on devices has been restricted due to their limited public availability and large resource footprint. Our work addresses these issues by publicly releasing a collection of paralinguistic speech models that are small and near state-of-the-art performance. Our approach is based on knowledge distillation, and our models are distilled on public data only. We explore different architectures and thoroughly evaluate our models on the Non-Semantic Speech (NOSS) benchmark. Our largest distilled model is less than 15% the size of the original model (314MB vs 2.2GB), achieves over 96% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks, and is trained on 6.5% the data. The smallest model is 1% in size (22MB) and achieves over 90% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks. Our models outperform the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 model on 6 of 7 tasks, and our smallest model outperforms the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 on both emotion recognition tasks despite being 7% the size.

papers_seen.author: Humphrey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Deploying Deep Learning Models in Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile technique for compressing deep neural networks and improving their practical deployability. By enabling smaller "student" networks to learn from larger "teacher" models, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems across diverse domains and hardware constraints. This approach achieves significant model compression ratios while maintaining or even improving performance, making it invaluable for applications requiring efficient inference, interpretability, and resource-constrained deployment. The technique extends beyond simple model compression to encompass diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, reinforcement learning, and federated learning, demonstrating its fundamental importance in modern machine learning practice.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Transferring Knowledge for Efficient Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining performance. This approach transfers knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student model, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices. Model compression through distillation has proven effective across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning. This paper surveys the principles, methods, and applications of knowledge distillation and related compression techniques in deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Knowledge Distillation for CTR Prediction
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, deep learning-based models have been widely studied for click-through rate (CTR) prediction and lead to improved prediction accuracy in many industrial applications. However, current research focuses primarily on building complex network architectures to better capture sophisticated feature interactions and dynamic user behaviors. The increased model complexity may slow down online inference and hinder its adoption in real-time applications. Instead, our work targets at a new model training strategy based on knowledge distillation (KD). KD is a teacher-student learning framework to transfer knowledge learned from a teacher model to a student model. The KD strategy not only allows us to simplify the student model as a vanilla DNN model but also achieves significant accuracy improvements over the state-of-the-art teacher models. The benefits thus motivate us to further explore the use of a powerful ensemble of teachers for more accurate student model training. We also propose some novel techniques to facilitate ensembled CTR prediction, including teacher gating and early stopping by distillation loss. We conduct comprehensive experiments against 12 existing models and across three industrial datasets. Both offline and online A/B testing results show the effectiveness of our KD-based training strategy.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Techniques, and Caveats
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a niche compression trick into a broad set of methods that enable deploying high-performing but compact models across vision, language, and other domains. KD techniques operate at different levels (logits, feature maps, intermediate layers) and can be combined with pruning, quantization, or domain adaptation strategies to meet latency, memory, privacy, and cross-domain generalization constraints. When applied with task-aware design and attention to optimization and data constraints, KD yields substantial practical gains for real-world systems; however, mismatches between teacher and student capacities, data availability, and optimization dynamics require careful method selection and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Layer-aware, Multi-source, and Data-efficient Knowledge Distillation for Compressing Pretrained NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central tool for compressing large pre-trained language models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Effective compression requires going beyond matching final logits: it benefits from transferring intermediate representations, adapting to domain shifts, leveraging multiple reliable supervision sources, and handling cases where original training data cannot be shared. I argue that a practical, high-performing distillation pipeline for NLP should (1) align teacher and student internal representations with flexible many-to-many mappings, (2) weight and fuse signals from multiple teachers by confidence, (3) include domain-aware adaptation before distillation, and (4) incorporate data-free or privacy-preserving distillation options when necessary. Combining these elements yields compact models that retain much of the teacher’s capabilities while meeting deployment and privacy goals.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically proven approach for compressing large neural networks into efficient models suitable for deployment. Across modalities and tasks — from vision and speech to NLP and retrieval — KD can be implemented through multiple, complementary mechanisms (soft-label supervision, feature mimicry, layer-wise alignment, teacher adaptation, and online co-training) to trade off capacity, compute, and data constraints while retaining much of the teacher performance. Practical KD pipelines benefit from task-aware selection of distilled signals, efficient label generation or online schemes to reduce teacher cost, and teacher/student co-design to close the capacity gap between models.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: MixKD: Towards Efficient Distillation of Large-scale Language Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale language models have recently demonstrated impressive empirical performance. Nevertheless, the improved results are attained at the price of bigger models, more power consumption, and slower inference, which hinder their applicability to low-resource (both memory and computation) platforms. Knowledge distillation (KD) has been demonstrated as an effective framework for compressing such big models. However, large-scale neural network systems are prone to memorize training instances, and thus tend to make inconsistent predictions when the data distribution is altered slightly. Moreover, the student model has few opportunities to request useful information from the teacher model when there is limited task-specific data available. To address these issues, we propose MixKD, a data-agnostic distillation framework that leverages mixup, a simple yet efficient data augmentation approach, to endow the resulting model with stronger generalization ability. Concretely, in addition to the original training examples, the student model is encouraged to mimic the teacher's behavior on the linear interpolation of example pairs as well. We prove from a theoretical perspective that under reasonable conditions MixKD gives rise to a smaller gap between the generalization error and the empirical error. To verify its effectiveness, we conduct experiments on the GLUE benchmark, where MixKD consistently leads to significant gains over the standard KD training, and outperforms several competitive baselines. Experiments under a limited-data setting and ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, powerful models into smaller, faster models by transferring information beyond hard labels. In NLP and broader deep learning, KD has been applied to pre-trained transformers, sequence models, ensembles, and cross-modal architectures using techniques that include soft-label matching, intermediate feature supervision, progressive module replacement, architecture search, data augmentation, and adversarial sample selection. These methods trade off fidelity to the teacher, student capacity, and inference efficiency; recent work emphasizes task-adaptive compression, improved feature alignment, and tailoring teachers to be more 'student-friendly' to maximize transfer. Empirical results show that carefully designed KD procedures can retain much of the teacher's performance while reducing model size and latency, enabling deployment in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Mitigating Gender Bias in Distilled Language Models via Counterfactual Role Reversal
papers_seen.abstract: Language models excel at generating coherent text, and model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation have enabled their use in resource-constrained settings. However, these models can be biased in multiple ways, including the unfounded association of male and female genders with gender-neutral professions. Therefore, knowledge distillation without any fairness constraints may preserve or exaggerate the teacher model's biases onto the distilled model. To this end, we present a novel approach to mitigate gender disparity in text generation by learning a fair model during knowledge distillation. We propose two modifications to the base knowledge distillation based on counterfactual role reversal$\unicode{x2014}$modifying teacher probabilities and augmenting the training set. We evaluate gender polarity across professions in open-ended text generated from the resulting distilled and finetuned GPT$\unicode{x2012}$2 models and demonstrate a substantial reduction in gender disparity with only a minor compromise in utility. Finally, we observe that language models that reduce gender polarity in language generation do not improve embedding fairness or downstream classification fairness.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted training paradigm that enables the compression of large neural networks by transferring knowledge from a high-capacity teacher model to a more efficient student model. This approach has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and recommendation systems. By leveraging teacher guidance during training, knowledge distillation achieves significant reductions in model size and computational cost while maintaining or even improving student model performance, making it essential for deploying neural networks on resource-constrained devices and enabling practical real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have matured into a diverse set of methods for producing smaller, faster, and sometimes more robust models from larger teachers. Approaches span from soft-label and internal-representation transfer to data-free distillation, federated/distilled training for privacy and communication efficiency, and task-adaptive architecture search for large pretrained language models. Empirical work shows KD can improve inference efficiency with limited accuracy loss, transfer adversarial robustness, and enable effective low-precision and task-specific compressed models, while theoretical analyses and algorithmic variants clarify when and why distillation helps.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Synthesis of Recent Advances
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining predictive performance. These methods involve transferring knowledge from larger, more complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, practical applications, and recent innovations in knowledge distillation across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains like object detection and graph neural networks. The review highlights mechanisms that enable successful knowledge transfer, strategies for handling heterogeneous model architectures, data-free distillation approaches, and applications to federated learning and multi-modal learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Promises and Practicalities of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while preserving performance. Empirical successes span vision, language, graph, and retrieval tasks, and variants include multi-teacher, self-distillation, feature-level and adversarial formulations. However, distillation is not a panacea: its benefits depend on how knowledge is represented (soft targets vs. internal features), on the student–teacher interaction mechanisms, and on data- and deployment-specific constraints (e.g., heterogeneous clients or low-frequency tokens). This article argues that KD is a powerful and flexible tool when combined with principled modifications — such as internal-representation distillation, projector ensembles, multi-teacher curricula, improved data augmentation, and task-aware distillation losses — but that practitioners must attend to these factors to realize reliable compression and generalization gains.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Strategy for Efficient Deep Learning: Enabling Practical Deployment of Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial technique for model compression and efficient deployment of deep neural networks across diverse domains. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a fundamentally important approach for reducing computational overhead and memory requirements of state-of-the-art neural models while maintaining competitive performance. Through systematic application in computer vision, natural language processing, and other domains, distillation has demonstrated remarkable effectiveness in creating compact student models that can operate within practical resource constraints. The technique's versatility, combined with its ability to achieve substantial efficiency gains with minimal accuracy loss, establishes it as an indispensable tool for the practical deployment of neural networks in resource-limited environments.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Techniques and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing, enabling the creation of efficient student models that learn from larger, more complex teacher networks. This approach addresses the fundamental challenge of deploying sophisticated neural models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. The methodology spans multiple domains including computer vision, NLP tasks, and graph neural networks, demonstrating its versatility and effectiveness across different problem spaces. Beyond basic compression, knowledge distillation has been extended to address important concerns such as adversarial robustness, privacy preservation, fairness mitigation, and domain generalization, establishing it as a foundational technique in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Distilling Object Detectors with Fine-grained Feature Imitation
papers_seen.abstract: State-of-the-art CNN based recognition models are often computationally prohibitive to deploy on low-end devices. A promising high level approach tackling this limitation is knowledge distillation, which let small student model mimic cumbersome teacher model's output to get improved generalization. However, related methods mainly focus on simple task of classification while do not consider complex tasks like object detection. We show applying the vanilla knowledge distillation to detection model gets minor gain. To address the challenge of distilling knowledge in detection model, we propose a fine-grained feature imitation method exploiting the cross-location discrepancy of feature response. Our intuition is that detectors care more about local near object regions. Thus the discrepancy of feature response on the near object anchor locations reveals important information of how teacher model tends to generalize. We design a novel mechanism to estimate those locations and let student model imitate the teacher on them to get enhanced performance. We first validate the idea on a developed lightweight toy detector which carries simplest notion of current state-of-the-art anchor based detection models on challenging KITTI dataset, our method generates up to 15% boost of mAP for the student model compared to the non-imitated counterpart. We then extensively evaluate the method with Faster R-CNN model under various scenarios with common object detection benchmark of Pascal VOC and COCO, imitation alleviates up to 74% performance drop of student model compared to teacher. Codes released at https://github.com/twangnh/Distilling-Object-Detectors

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-used technique for compressing neural networks and transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. This approach has been successfully applied across multiple domains including neural machine translation, language models, graph neural networks, and speech processing. The technique enables deployment of high-performing models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy through various knowledge transfer mechanisms and distillation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have become central to deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research spans practical recipes (logit matching, feature and layer-wise matching, projector modules), structural compression (architectural transforms, channel/filter reduction), and specialized strategies for NLP models (layer mapping for transformers and task-aware layer selection). Recent work also addresses learning dynamics and theory for wide networks, multi-teacher and meta-learned teaching, and scenarios with limited or no access to original training data. Empirical results show that careful choice of distillation targets, alignment mechanisms, and teacher-student curricula can yield compact models that retain strong performance on downstream tasks while enabling faster inference and smaller memory footprints. Open challenges include task-specific selection of distilled knowledge, robustness and generalization across distributions, and principled guidelines for architecture-aware distillation in transformers.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD includes techniques that use teacher output distributions, intermediate representations, contrastive objectives, data augmentation, and multi-stage or multi-teacher pipelines. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can improve student generalization, but success depends on optimization, data, augmentation, and how knowledge is represented and matched. Advances include representation-level contrastive distillation, data-mixing augmentations for more robust transfer, meta-learned teachers, and task-specific pipelines (e.g., NLP QA, graph learning) that adapt student architectures to preserve domain priors. Together, these results highlight practical best practices (careful choice of targets, augmentation, and teacher-student interaction) and point to open problems in aligning representations, handling distribution shifts, and designing teachers that teach effectively for resource-constrained deployments.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Embracing the Dark Knowledge: Domain Generalization Using Regularized Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Though convolutional neural networks are widely used in different tasks, lack of generalization capability in the absence of sufficient and representative data is one of the challenges that hinder their practical application. In this paper, we propose a simple, effective, and plug-and-play training strategy named Knowledge Distillation for Domain Generalization (KDDG) which is built upon a knowledge distillation framework with the gradient filter as a novel regularization term. We find that both the ``richer dark knowledge" from the teacher network, as well as the gradient filter we proposed, can reduce the difficulty of learning the mapping which further improves the generalization ability of the model. We also conduct experiments extensively to show that our framework can significantly improve the generalization capability of deep neural networks in different tasks including image classification, segmentation, reinforcement learning by comparing our method with existing state-of-the-art domain generalization techniques. Last but not the least, we propose to adopt two metrics to analyze our proposed method in order to better understand how our proposed method benefits the generalization capability of deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Enhancing Student Model Performance Through Teacher-Guided Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or even improving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from a well-trained teacher model to a lightweight student model through various mechanisms including soft target matching, intermediate layer alignment, and task-aware filtering. Applications span across natural language processing, computer vision, and domain-specific tasks, addressing critical deployment challenges related to latency, computational resources, and model size constraints in real-world production environments.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: MixKD: Towards Efficient Distillation of Large-scale Language Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale language models have recently demonstrated impressive empirical performance. Nevertheless, the improved results are attained at the price of bigger models, more power consumption, and slower inference, which hinder their applicability to low-resource (both memory and computation) platforms. Knowledge distillation (KD) has been demonstrated as an effective framework for compressing such big models. However, large-scale neural network systems are prone to memorize training instances, and thus tend to make inconsistent predictions when the data distribution is altered slightly. Moreover, the student model has few opportunities to request useful information from the teacher model when there is limited task-specific data available. To address these issues, we propose MixKD, a data-agnostic distillation framework that leverages mixup, a simple yet efficient data augmentation approach, to endow the resulting model with stronger generalization ability. Concretely, in addition to the original training examples, the student model is encouraged to mimic the teacher's behavior on the linear interpolation of example pairs as well. We prove from a theoretical perspective that under reasonable conditions MixKD gives rise to a smaller gap between the generalization error and the empirical error. To verify its effectiveness, we conduct experiments on the GLUE benchmark, where MixKD consistently leads to significant gains over the standard KD training, and outperforms several competitive baselines. Experiments under a limited-data setting and ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: No One Left Behind: Inclusive Federated Learning over Heterogeneous Devices
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is an important paradigm for training global models from decentralized data in a privacy-preserving way. Existing FL methods usually assume the global model can be trained on any participating client. However, in real applications, the devices of clients are usually heterogeneous, and have different computing power. Although big models like BERT have achieved huge success in AI, it is difficult to apply them to heterogeneous FL with weak clients. The straightforward solutions like removing the weak clients or using a small model to fit all clients will lead to some problems, such as under-representation of dropped clients and inferior accuracy due to data loss or limited model representation ability. In this work, we propose InclusiveFL, a client-inclusive federated learning method to handle this problem. The core idea of InclusiveFL is to assign models of different sizes to clients with different computing capabilities, bigger models for powerful clients and smaller ones for weak clients. We also propose an effective method to share the knowledge among multiple local models with different sizes. In this way, all the clients can participate in the model learning in FL, and the final model can be big and powerful enough. Besides, we propose a momentum knowledge distillation method to better transfer knowledge in big models on powerful clients to the small models on weak clients. Extensive experiments on many real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in learning accurate models from clients with heterogeneous devices under the FL framework.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Methods, Applications, and Empirical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a teacher network to a student network. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments such as mobile and edge devices. The field encompasses diverse methodologies ranging from feature-level distillation to cross-modal approaches, with applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning. Recent research has advanced both theoretical understanding and practical implementations of knowledge distillation, demonstrating significant improvements in model compression while maintaining predictive performance.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile approach for both model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a superior alternative to traditional compression methods because it enables effective compression while maintaining model performance, facilitates transfer of complex learned representations across architectures, and proves applicable across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and reinforcement learning. Unlike methods that simply reduce model parameters without guidance, knowledge distillation leverages teacher-student frameworks to encode valuable "dark knowledge" that improves generalization and produces more robust, efficient models.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, more efficient students while retaining much of the teachers' performance. Recent work expands the KD toolkit beyond matching soft logits to include feature- and layer-level mimicry, task-aware selection of teacher knowledge, data-free and multi-teacher strategies, and augmentation-driven improvements. Practical advances target domain-specific challenges in language models and cross-modal systems, emphasize efficient training and deployment on heterogeneous hardware, and reinterpret KD as a form of regularization that can sometimes be partially replaced or simulated. This review synthesizes these directions and highlights recurring design principles for effective distillation in both NLP and general deep learning settings.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Efficient and Robust NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a unifying approach for producing smaller, faster, and often more robust models for NLP and deep learning broadly. When combined with architecture search, layer-wise matching, data-centric techniques, and privacy-aware protocols, distillation enables task-adaptive compression, domain adaptation, and practical deployment under latency, memory, and regulatory constraints. However, the benefits of distillation depend on how knowledge is represented, which data and augmentations are used during transfer, and whether the distillation procedure is aligned with downstream tasks; careful method design—rather than blind teacher-student pairing—is therefore required to realize its full promise.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models by transferring knowledge from teacher models. This approach has become increasingly important as deep learning models grow larger and more computationally demanding, yet deployment requirements necessitate efficient, lightweight alternatives. Model compression through knowledge distillation encompasses diverse methodologies across computer vision, NLP, and multimodal domains, enabling practical deployment on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques have matured into a diverse set of theoretical and practical approaches for producing smaller, faster, or more specialized models from larger ones. Work in this area ranges from formal analyses of when and why distillation helps, to engineering advances that reduce runtime cost, enable training without original data, transfer across modalities, improve robustness and privacy, and tailor distilled models for downstream tasks or heterogeneous deployment environments. Practical methods include mimicking logits, matching intermediate representations or attention, progressively replacing modules, using student-focused filtering of teacher signals, and leveraging data augmentation or online collaboration between models. Emerging directions emphasize theoretical understanding, task-aware selection of distilled information, privacy-preserving or data-free pipelines, and retaining adversarial robustness while reducing model size.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Preserving Privacy in Federated Learning with Ensemble Cross-Domain Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where local nodes collaboratively train a central model while the training data remains decentralized. Existing FL methods typically share model parameters or employ co-distillation to address the issue of unbalanced data distribution. However, they suffer from communication bottlenecks. More importantly, they risk privacy leakage. In this work, we develop a privacy preserving and communication efficient method in a FL framework with one-shot offline knowledge distillation using unlabeled, cross-domain public data. We propose a quantized and noisy ensemble of local predictions from completely trained local models for stronger privacy guarantees without sacrificing accuracy. Based on extensive experiments on image classification and text classification tasks, we show that our privacy-preserving method outperforms baseline FL algorithms with superior performance in both accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Essential Techniques for Practical Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful approach for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and natural language processing. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is an indispensable technique for deploying large-scale pre-trained models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. The method effectively addresses the critical challenge of reducing computational overhead and memory requirements without sacrificing accuracy, making it essential for real-world applications where inference speed and efficiency are paramount.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Releasing Graph Neural Networks with Differential Privacy Guarantees
papers_seen.abstract: With the increasing popularity of graph neural networks (GNNs) in several sensitive applications like healthcare and medicine, concerns have been raised over the privacy aspects of trained GNNs. More notably, GNNs are vulnerable to privacy attacks, such as membership inference attacks, even if only black-box access to the trained model is granted. We propose PrivGNN, a privacy-preserving framework for releasing GNN models in a centralized setting. Assuming an access to a public unlabeled graph, PrivGNN provides a framework to release GNN models trained explicitly on public data along with knowledge obtained from the private data in a privacy preserving manner. PrivGNN combines the knowledge-distillation framework with the two noise mechanisms, random subsampling, and noisy labeling, to ensure rigorous privacy guarantees. We theoretically analyze our approach in the Renyi differential privacy framework. Besides, we show the solid experimental performance of our method compared to several baselines adapted for graph-structured data. Our code is available at https://github.com/iyempissy/privGnn.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Critical Technique for Deep Learning Model Compression and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large deep learning models while maintaining performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student models, enabling efficient deployment across diverse applications. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential strategy for addressing the trade-off between model complexity and practical deployment requirements in both computer vision and natural language processing domains.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Embracing the Dark Knowledge: Domain Generalization Using Regularized Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Though convolutional neural networks are widely used in different tasks, lack of generalization capability in the absence of sufficient and representative data is one of the challenges that hinder their practical application. In this paper, we propose a simple, effective, and plug-and-play training strategy named Knowledge Distillation for Domain Generalization (KDDG) which is built upon a knowledge distillation framework with the gradient filter as a novel regularization term. We find that both the ``richer dark knowledge" from the teacher network, as well as the gradient filter we proposed, can reduce the difficulty of learning the mapping which further improves the generalization ability of the model. We also conduct experiments extensively to show that our framework can significantly improve the generalization capability of deep neural networks in different tasks including image classification, segmentation, reinforcement learning by comparing our method with existing state-of-the-art domain generalization techniques. Last but not the least, we propose to adopt two metrics to analyze our proposed method in order to better understand how our proposed method benefits the generalization capability of deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Enabling Multimodal Generation on CLIP via Vision-Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The recent large-scale vision-language pre-training (VLP) of dual-stream architectures (e.g., CLIP) with a tremendous amount of image-text pair data, has shown its superiority on various multimodal alignment tasks. Despite its success, the resulting models are not capable of multimodal generative tasks due to the weak text encoder. To tackle this problem, we propose to augment the dual-stream VLP model with a textual pre-trained language model (PLM) via vision-language knowledge distillation (VLKD), enabling the capability for multimodal generation. VLKD is pretty data- and computation-efficient compared to the pre-training from scratch. Experimental results show that the resulting model has strong zero-shot performance on multimodal generation tasks, such as open-ended visual question answering and image captioning. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\times$ fewer parameters. Furthermore, the original textual language understanding and generation ability of the PLM is maintained after VLKD, which makes our model versatile for both multimodal and unimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques provide practical paths to deploy large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Recent work spans strategies that (1) compress by transferring softened outputs or intermediate representations from large teachers to smaller students, (2) pre-train compact architectures instead of only compressing post-hoc, (3) adapt distillation to task specifics (e.g., detection, generation, ranking), (4) enable distillation without access to original training data, and (5) combine KD with quantization, pruning, and data augmentation to improve robustness and efficiency. Empirical evidence shows that carefully designed distillation losses, data strategies, and teacher-student curricula can preserve much of teacher performance while greatly reducing model size, latency, and memory footprint. Practical trade-offs include the need for task-specific treatment (feature imitation, permutation-invariant alignment), sensitivity to the teacher’s training regime, and opportunities where teacher-free or self-distillation variants can match or exceed classic teacher-student pipelines.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation for Deep Models and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful family of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster, and often more interpretable models. When applied thoughtfully—matching architectures, choosing which teacher signals to transfer, and adapting to task- or data-specific properties—KD can preserve most of the teacher's performance while substantially reducing inference cost. However, indiscriminate application of distillation can harm performance (for example by overfitting to teacher errors or erasing useful data complexity); successful KD therefore combines algorithmic innovations (layer/feature matching, progressive replacement, adaptive search) with data-aware strategies (selective sample distillation, mixing raw and distilled data) and sometimes self-distillation to close remaining gaps.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression approaches transfer information from larger or differently-abled models to smaller, faster, or modality-restricted models. Methods vary from matching final soft logits to mimicking intermediate representations, mapping layers across architectures, adversarially synthesizing training data, and adapting distillation to distributed or heterogeneous-device settings. Empirical and theoretical work highlights trade-offs between simplicity, effectiveness, data availability, and task-specificity, and suggests design patterns for effective compression across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Fundamental Approach to Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a transformative technique for compressing neural networks while maintaining predictive performance. By enabling knowledge transfer from large teacher models to compact student networks, distillation addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential methodology for practical machine learning deployment, offering significant advantages in model size reduction, computational efficiency, and accessibility across diverse application domains from natural language processing to computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have become central to deploying high-performing deep models under computational, memory, privacy, and latency constraints. Work in this area spans traditional teacher→student soft-target distillation, distillation of internal representations, data-free or zero-shot approaches for when training data are unavailable, online and mutual distillation among peers, multi-teacher and ensemble-based strategies, and adaptations for domain shifts and task-specific requirements (e.g., non-autoregressive translation). Empirical findings emphasize that distillation often reduces training data complexity and transfers information most effectively when methods account for representation mismatch, data generation or augmentation, teacher–student capacity differences, and the distributional specifics of the task. Practical trends favor hybrid pipelines that combine soft-targets with representation matching, selective use of raw or synthesized data, and scalable online/ensemble procedures to support large datasets and heterogeneous deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques transform large, costly models into smaller, faster, or more private models while retaining much of the original performance. Across modalities and tasks, distillation has been applied to compress vision and language models, transfer cross-modal or privileged information, enable deployment under latency and memory constraints, and preserve privacy in distributed settings. Key directions include distillation of logits (soft labels), feature- or attention-level distillation, self-distillation, data-free or zero-shot approaches, and architecture-aware compression. Empirical results show that when carefully designed—often combining distillation with pruning or architecture search—student models can approach teacher accuracy, gain robustness, or enable capabilities (e.g., multimodal generation) previously unavailable to the smaller model. Important open problems remain in data heterogeneity, robustness transfer, and principled teacher-student design for diverse deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression techniques enable the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. These approaches have demonstrated significant success across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and speech processing, achieving substantial reductions in model size and computational cost while maintaining competitive accuracy levels. This synthesis explores the diverse methodologies, theoretical foundations, and practical applications of knowledge distillation and compression techniques in modern deep learning systems.

To address these issues, we propose MixKD, a data-agnostic distillation framework that leverages mixup, a simple yet efficient data augmentation approach, to endow the resulting model with stronger generalization ability. Concretely, in addition to the original training examples, the student model is encouraged to mimic the teacher's behavior on the linear interpolation of example pairs as well. We prove from a theoretical perspective that under reasonable conditions MixKD gives rise to a smaller gap between the generalization error and the empirical error. To verify its effectiveness, we conduct experiments on the GLUE benchmark, where MixKD consistently leads to significant gains over the standard KD training, and outperforms several competitive baselines. Experiments under a limited-data setting and ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach."}, {'author': 'Ferrell', 'year': 2018, 'title': 'AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence', 'abstract': 'Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.'}, {'author': 'Munoz', 'year': 2021, 'title': 'Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks', 'abstract': 'Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.'}, {'author': 'Williams', 'year': 2018, 'title': 'Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation', 'abstract': 'Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.'}, {'author': 'Harrell', 'year': 2022, 'title': 'No One Left Behind: Inclusive Federated Learning over Heterogeneous Devices', 'abstract': 'Federated learning (FL) is an important paradigm for training global models from decentralized data in a privacy-preserving way. Existing FL methods usually assume the global model can be trained on any participating client. However, in real applications, the devices of clients are usually heterogeneous, and have different computing power. Although big models like BERT have achieved huge success in AI, it is difficult to apply them to heterogeneous FL with weak clients. The straightforward solutions like removing the weak clients or using a small model to fit all clients will lead to some problems, such as under-representation of dropped clients and inferior accuracy due to data loss or limited model representation ability. In this work, we propose InclusiveFL, a client-inclusive federated learning method to handle this problem. The core idea of InclusiveFL is to assign models of different sizes to clients with different computing capabilities, bigger models for powerful clients and smaller ones for weak clients. We also propose an effective method to share the knowledge among multiple local models with different sizes. In this way, all the clients can participate in the model learning in FL, and the final model can be big and powerful enough. Besides, we propose a momentum knowledge distillation method to better transfer knowledge in big models on powerful clients to the small models on weak clients. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html."}, {'author': 'Fowler', 'year': 2023, 'title': 'Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches', 'abstract': "Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, more efficient students while retaining much of the teachers' performance. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\\times$ fewer parameters. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential methodology for practical machine learning deployment, offering significant advantages in model size reduction, computational efficiency, and accessibility across diverse application domains from natural language processing to computer vision.'}, {'author': 'Ramirez', 'year': 2017, 'title': 'Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets', 'abstract': "The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression."}, {'author': 'Abbott', 'year': 2024, 'title': 'A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP', 'abstract': 'Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have become central to deploying high-performing deep models under computational, memory, privacy, and latency constraints.
